hook: Water Board's target: a *tanker-free* Hyderabad by end-2028
hook_b: Water Board's target: a *tanker-free* Hyderabad by end-2028
tldr: HMWSSB MD K Ashok Reddy told TOI readers the plan hinges on Godavari Phase II and III adding 320 MGD by end-2027.

beats.what: Godavari Phase II and III are to add 320 MGD by end-2027, aiming at daily supply to all CURE-area homes.
beats.why: Peripheral areas like Kollur, Gachibowli, Kokapet and Neopolis still lean on expensive private tankers.
beats.care: If the network reaches these areas, households would not need to pay for private tankers.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: TOI: 15 more filling stations are proposed for this summer, and an order now bars illegal groundwater extraction by bulk non-domestic users.

cards.q: Tanker-free by 2028: how does that sound for your area?

qs: Which neighbourhoods will get daily supply first once Godavari water arrives?
How will the board track whether tanker bookings actually fall?

facts.t: HMWSSB runs a *15,000-km* pipe network, with pipes from 2 to 50 years old.

viz.verdict: A long-term target, tied to Godavari works
A long-term target, tied to Godavari works
More tankers registered before the network catches up

learn.t: CURE = Core Urban Region Economy, the area inside the ORR under the Telangana Rising 2047 plan.

watch: Whether Godavari Phase II and III are commissioned by end-2027 as planned.

sources.name: Times of India
sources.title: Hyderabad aims to become tanker-free city by 2028

fact: Hyderabad Water Board targets a *tanker-free* city by the end of 2028.
twist: Right now *1,500 tankers* and 96 filling stations serve the CURE area, with 300 more tankers to be registered.
